extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (AP wire audience), news editors
extracted.subtask_description: Associated Press wire copy reporting on Korean War military actions, United Nations diplomacy, U.S. Congressional matters, and Korean domestic politics; intended as daily news for newspapers and general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.N. staff regulations - complete employment disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: U.N. staff regulations require an applicant to have made a complete statement of past employment and that a wilful misstatement is grounds for [dismissal].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers of the U.N. questioned Wallach on personnel matters; a willful misstatement can be grounds for action (dismissal). The regulation is invoked when investigating alleged subversion or communism among Secretariat staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republic of Korea (ROK) constitutional timing for presidential election
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the Republic of Korea constitution, the election for president and vice-president should not take place later than 30 days before expiration of the term of the outgoing president.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhee was sworn in on June 23, 1948 but did not officially take office until July 15; opponents demanded an election by a certain date and supporters sought to delay until July 15. The constitutional timing governs when the Assembly must hold the election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative passage threshold for constitutional amendment (ROK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Passage of the compromise constitutional amendment requires 122 votes, a two-thirds majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A boycott by 39 anti-administration members made it virtually impossible to reach the two-thirds majority required, blocking the compromise amendments intended to resolve the political crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and loyalty-check prerequisite for release of civilian internees
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of civilian internees has been delayed because of the difficulty of performing dependable screening and investigation to determine that they are, in fact, loyal ROK citizens; 'a thorough and complete loyalty check' is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities justified the delay by saying such loyalty checks are a precaution fully justified by later developments; only after such screening are internees released and returned to home areas with assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard package for released civilian internees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each released civilian will be given a 30-day supply of rations, a shirt, blanket, pair of trousers, underwear, shoes, two pairs of socks, a hat or cap and a raincoat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The U.N. Civil Assistance Commission for Korea will assist in returning internees to their home areas; the package is intended to aid reintegration and help the ROK economy by returning manpower to farms and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of voluntary repatriation of prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: The voluntary repatriation principle: prisoners held by either side should be allowed to return to their home country of their own free will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle was cited as key in truce negotiations; Communist negotiators labeled allied proposals for voluntary repatriation 'unfair' while U.S. negotiators noted historical Soviet advocacy of voluntary repatriation during World War II as precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal for ratification of the 1925 Geneva Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal urging states to sign and ratify the 1925 Geneva Protocol outlawing poison gas and bacteriological (biological) weapons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. and other delegates urged ratification as a response to charges of germ warfare; debate was expected and some delegations (e.g., Russia) were likely to resist or veto procedural moves. The appeal was presented as a diplomatic measure to isolate propaganda and reaffirm norm against chemical/biological weapons.
